channel.title: STLACCESS — FDM Scale Math
channel.description: FDM-focused scale math and conversion percentages from STLACCESS.

item.title: Tabletop Gaming with FDM: Best Printers, Settings, and Models for Minis and Terrain
item.description: FDM printers and slicer settings that actually work for tabletop miniatures and terrain — CoreXY vs bed-slinger picks across budgets, 0.2mm nozzle tuning, and a mini-vs-terrain settings cheat sheet.

item.title: The Ultimate FDM Filament Guide: Materials, Nozzles, and Strength Tuning
item.description: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, TPU, nylon composites, and metal-filled filaments — how to choose the right plastic, match it to the correct nozzle, and avoid clogs, warping, and shredded spools.

item.title: FDM vs Resin vs SLS 3D Printing: Which Technology Fits Your Project?
item.description: A head-to-head look at FDM, resin/SLA, and SLS printing — how each melts, cures, or sinters material, plus detail, strength, safety, and cost comparisons with a decision matrix for props, miniatures, and functional parts.

item.title: How to Sand, Paint, and Post-Process FDM 3D Prints Like a Pro
item.description: Turn rough, ridged FDM prints into smooth, professional parts — surgical support removal, the 120-to-400 grit progression, filler priming and the spray-sand-repeat cycle, then painting and locking in your FDM miniatures.

item.title: What Is FDM 3D Printing? A Beginner's Guide to How It Works
item.description: FDM vs FFF explained, the extrusion process from STL to G-code to finished layers, the history from Stratasys to the 2009 patent expiry and RepRap boom, plus the real pros and cons of fused deposition modeling.

item.title: Arachne vs Classic Wall Generator: Which Is Sharper for Miniatures?
item.description: Arachne is supposed to make tighter details than the classic wall generator, but on test miniatures classic often prints fine detail sharper. A practical comparison for 28-32mm FDM prints.

item.title: Cura Tree Support Settings: How to Make Supports Easy to Remove
item.description: The exact Cura tree (organic) support settings for 3D printing miniatures that come off clean — Z distance, interface layers, branch distance and angle, and painting supports on manually.

item.title: FDM vs Resin 3D Printing for Miniatures: When to Switch
item.description: The honest resin vs FDM comparison for tabletop miniatures — detail, support removal, toxicity, speed, and which kinds of models each printer genuinely does better.

item.title: Real-World Objects to 28mm Scale: Feet to MM Conversion for 28mm WWII Platoon Wargames, the Classic Fantasy RPG & Historical
item.description: The formula I use to convert real-world heights to true 28mm miniature scale. Charts for humans, monsters, vehicles, and terrain for 28mm WWII platoon wargames, the classic fantasy RPG, and historical wargaming.

item.title: Resin2FDM: Convert Resin-Supported STLs to FDM-Ready in Blender
item.description: How to take a resin-presupported STL from any sculptor and make it print clean on an FDM printer using the Resin2FDM Blender add-on — split, assign, thicken supports, and slice for cleanup.

item.title: Best Budget 3D Printers for Tabletop Wargaming — FDM Terrrain & Vehicle Guide
item.description: Top budget FDM 3D printers for wargaming terrain, vehicles, and scatter. Sovol SV06 ACE, Creality Ender-3 V3 SE, Bambu Lab A1 Mini, and Elegoo Centauri Carbon compared.

item.title: How to Scale 28mm to 32mm (114.3% Slicer Percentage, Explained)
item.description: What percent for 28mm to 32mm? 114.3% with XYZ locked. The math behind the conversion, the exact slicer steps for Chitubox, Lychee, Cura, and PrusaSlicer, and how to verify it on a test print.

item.title: How to Downscale 32mm to 28mm (87.5% Slicer Percentage, Explained)
item.description: Shrink 32mm miniatures down to true 28mm scale with an 87.5% slicer percentage. Fits more minis on a resin plate and mixes classic fantasy RPG proxies into true-scale armies.

item.title: Classic Fantasy RPG Miniature Scale Guide — What Size Are Classic Fantasy RPG Minis?
item.description: What scale is the classic fantasy RPG? Medium humanoids are 28mm to the eyes on the 175cm baseline. The full classic fantasy RPG size chart: Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, Gargantuan with mini heights and base sizes.

item.title: 35mm Sci-Fi Mass-Battle Game Scale Guide — What Scale Are Its Miniatures?
item.description: Miniatures for the 35mm sci-fi mass-battle game are 35mm scale (1:47), measured to eye level at 35.7mm. Full height about 40mm. Exact slicer percentages to convert its STLs and proxies for space opera armies.

item.title: How to Measure a Miniature's Scale: Eye Level vs Top of Head Explained
item.description: How I measure miniature scale for 3D printing — eye level vs top of head, PARKSIDE digital calipers, and why the 175cm baseline works.

item.title: FDM Miniature Printing: Complete Guide to Layer Height, Nozzles, and Settings
item.description: Best FDM settings for tabletop miniatures — nozzles, layer heights, orientation tips, and post-processing for 28mm and 32mm models. Tested on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini.

item.title: Real-World Objects to 32mm Scale: Feet to MM Conversion (The Math Explained)
item.description: The formula I use to convert real-world heights to 32mm miniature scale. Charts for humans, horses, monsters, and terrain for the modern sci-fi epic wargame, the classic fantasy RPG, and 28mm WWII platoon wargames.

item.title: Upscaling 3D Prints: How Big Can You Enlarge a 32mm Miniature Before Losing Detail?
item.description: How much can you enlarge a 32mm miniature on FDM before losing detail? Layer line visibility, nozzle settings, and slicer tips for clean upscaling on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini.

item.title: How to Scale Miniatures in Chitubox & Lychee Slicer (Without Messing Up the Base)
item.description: Step-by-step guide to scaling STL files in Chitubox and Lychee. Lock aspect ratios, scale without stretching the base, and understand the unit conversion — from my own slicer.

item.title: Why Miniature Scales Use a 175cm Human Baseline
item.description: Most tabletop miniature scales are built around a 175cm (5'9) human. Here is why I chose that number for every STLACCESS scale conversion.
